**Lesson.** Round 83's referee asked that a check not borrow the quantity it tests, and each direct version found something the borrowed
one hid. With one energy the remainder halves, and the published top end turns out to be the idle kernels' floor. With the best assignment
and the sign, the fit's split tells a split from a cancellation, and shows the symmetric pair's "null cluster" still several thousand times
above the residual at τ = 10⁹. With the loop's own crossing, target 12's κ is known to lie above the path's; with kernel indices, the
sequence test needs no slope proxy. With the energy, the plateau is the two-sample interpolation, and following it back to s = 10⁻⁴
exposes a saddle on the sample c*: the flow's instability is λ ≈ 1.1·10⁴, and the run that "stays" on it does so only because LSODA's
backward differences damp an unstable mode at hλ > 2. When two solvers disagree, read the steps before trusting either.

**Lesson.** A scaling law needs a scaling experiment (the referee's lesson); a conjecture's slow branch needs a longer run. At K ≤ 80 the
τ²/v branch looked 2.4·10⁻⁴ off the formula and converging more slowly than K⁻²; at K = 160 it is 6.1·10⁻⁵ off, its excess steepening toward
K⁻², and D‴.61 explains why that branch is the slow one: its mass lies on the real axis, where the Peano kernel's transform approaches its
limit slowest near the branch point. The tests had a blind spot of their own: np.isclose's default absolute tolerance of 10⁻⁸ made seven
assertions on quantities near 10⁻¹³ pass whatever their values. A tolerance must be stated in the units of what it compares.

A6's 36 it holds 22 with a frame — the 10 the draft left out fitting the prediction too — and names 14 without one, which bound the claim. A
proved bound earns its place only against the trivial one (the series' first term beat the Fock bound wherever ρ > 0). And a check must be
computed in the arithmetic of what it checks: the precision check took a Decimal difference in Python's default 28-digit context and printed
the precisions themselves as the digits agreed; only a test that the check falls short of the precision caught it.

**Lesson.** A replay is not a forecast (the referee's lesson), and its informative nulls each drop one ingredient: here the replay without
the drift flags the leave's window in 0 of 33 runs, with the drift but another stretch of the same draw's noise in 3–4, and no threshold on
the drift alone comes near — a leave needs the drifted coefficient and the coming noise together. A gap in a set defined by a cut has to be
checked against the cut: a third of the counted gaps were the cut's. And a line that prints two lists sorted by different keys pairs them
wrongly: C9A's 16-period early alarm was printed beside another run; print each item with its own value. Case lists that no test pins (the
scan's grid, the windows, the draws) let a mutant change what was run while every test passes; pinning them against the raw kills seven such
mutants at once.

**Design.** One referee, not modifying the repository. D3ci: Proposition D‴.58 as revised after round 84, with its code and results at
4bc7b07 (`review/REVIEW_round88_D3ci.md`). The referee:

  at 642 digits), A6E at two (K, axis) pairs, and A5's rows, series and far rows, all bit-identical to the raw;
- recomputed A6's exact errors with its own nodes (Newton on the orthonormal recurrence), Christoffel weights and closed-form inner
  products (the ratio to the last bit, the errors to 25 digits, at 6 cells to K = 160), and B5's anchored ends and the rounded best end
  with its own exact evaluator (every double taken exactly, exp at 90 digits);
- refitted all 36 A6 limits with seven ansätze (the published L + c/K² + d/K³; L + b/K + c/K²; four-point with K⁻¹; half-integer
  powers; a free exponent; two-point K⁻² and K^{−3/2}), with the excess's local exponents and the cusp's 1/K coefficient;
- computed every A6 rule's Mehler-frame ratio ρ, and checked (ii)'s identities and the Laplace sketch's algebra against D‴.61;
- ran 46 single-point mutants of round 84's code in neither round-84 list, and re-ran round 84's own and its referee's survivors;
- searched the literature on scaled Gauss–Hermite rules, kernel quadrature and Hermite-space error analyses (four searches, snippets).

**Verdicts (D3ci).** Reproducibility is exact; every number of the round's new text traces to the md and the raw; (ii)'s identities, the
cusp's slope (1 − t²)/2 and the sketch's algebra are right; the cusp claim is strongly supported (the 1/K coefficient of ratio·t − 1
−0.250000 at τ/σ ≤ 1, −0.250003 at 2: e_K ∝ K^{1/4}t^K); the vσ*²/τ² branch is robust (the excess as K⁻², the limits within 10⁻⁷ of t(v)
by every ansatz matching it); round 84's issues are fixed. No major issue. Minors: the τ²/v branch's limits depend on the ansatz (−1.4·10⁻⁴
… +1.2·10⁻⁴ over seven, the uniform sign the K⁻² ansatz's); the rounded best end read as the double parameters' floor, which B5's own κ = ¼
end undercuts ten times; D58 does not cite D‴.61, its sketch's domain unstated and A6E "bounded" only above; 13 of 46 mutants survive both
checks, 3 of them changing published results on a rerun. Cosmetic: seven wording and printing items.

**Lesson.** An extrapolated limit is only as precise as its ansatz: where the excess's exponent still drifts, the fit's form sets the
deviation's size and sign, so print a second reasonable fit beside the first and report the spread — here the two bracket the conjecture
at every rule of the slow branch, which no single fit could show. A floor must be a lower bound; one rounded point is a scale (the
referee's lessons). A precision argument the tests exercise only where the default precision suffices is not pinned: test the job at its
hardest cell. And a count copied from a report must be recomputed: its table and its own check disagreed (13 and 10), and only the
script's printed count settled it.

is exponentially large off the imaginary axis —, and what is needed is domination, which holds for |η| < 1.8927 and on both axes up to 2

converges slowest on the real axis.

descent a conjecture: one exact identity on the circle, and an exact integral representation of He_K with a Gaussian bound, turned "the
saddle's rigorous treatment" into a short proof that rests on nothing from memory. And a test that monkeypatches the core function leaves
the wrapper's arithmetic untested: three of the four result-changing survivors sat around a patched `corner_ratio`.

**Lesson.** A window's verdict belongs to its start as well as its length (the referee's lesson): an alarm counts as the state's only if a
neighbouring start repeats it, the same loop from further back passes through it without leaving, and the leave lands where the replay
puts it — here none of the 12 isolated alarms passes the first test and C8R passes all 9 it covers; and the sets themselves keep a gap of
the basin at both neighbouring starts in only 6 of 13 windows. A null its authors call powerless cannot prove an ingredient absent. And a
summary over a list that can be empty (a band without multi-band windows, alarms only in runs that never left) must say so rather than fail.

domination condition holds on the whole disc |η| ≤ 1.8927 (branch and bound); all eight round-91 issues resolved. No major issue. Minors:
**the alias rate beyond the disc and its threshold 1.8637 were wrong** — a real stationary-phase point under a modulus varying on the same
exponential scale; the first alias is the second saddle of I_K's integrand on |ζ| = 1/√2, rate (5/8)y² − log y − ½ − (3/2)log 2, zero
1.8589, matched by Prony fits to 5 digits while two-point slopes oscillate —; "Λ⁺ attained" only where |Re σ| > 1; the condition's closed
form and a computer-assisted check in place of the grid; the proviso missing in New, and (b) on |η| < 1 and (c) undersold. Cosmetic: the
band below s = 1/|η| and Ω's openness; the rounded values up (r* 0.805257, 9.2699); the ellipse for every K, I_K zero-free, the σ in
(τ²σ²/σ*², τ²), "conjecture Q" in the md; three raw-only mutants.

**Lesson.** A stationary phase is not a saddle when the modulus varies on the same exponential scale (the referee's lesson), and two-point
slopes of an oscillating sequence measure nothing: fit the recurrence over consecutive K. Reduce an inequality to closed form before
gridding it: its supremum was explicit, and a branch and bound then covers the whole disc and shows the quoted margins sat on the proved
axis. And an entire integrand's path is free: where the straight segment fails, a path through the valleys of the bound's sublevel set
keeps the same main term — the obstruction was the path's, not the limit's.

rounded toward safety.

## Round 95 (adversarial review of Proposition D‴.61 as revised after round 93, 2026-11-01)

**Design.** One referee, not modifying the repository. D3cp: Proposition D‴.61 as revised after round 93 — the alias rate corrected,
the domination condition in closed form with a branch and bound, the deformed Duhamel path — at the round-93 commit
(`review/REVIEW_round95_D3cp.md`). The referee:
- regenerated the md byte for byte, ran the 26 tests, and recomputed 27 jobs and parts bit-identically, every new part-D job included;
- re-derived the deformed-path argument (the bound F along the path, the band near |σ| = 1, compactness off the ball, Laplace's method on
  the ball's segment) and the closed form's candidate set;
- rechecked all 402,664 branch-and-bound leaves at 40 digits, and probed `bound_sup` on boxes away from the leaves;
- computed c_K exactly to K = 312 and fitted λ₁ by Prony's method; scanned 222 points of the annulus with the valley check under grid
  refinement, 4-connectivity and steepest-descent seeds;

control (a bump the check must see, a bound it must use) is what turns an "equivalent on the data" survivor into a tested one.

**Lesson.** Prove a step that two lines prove: the chord's condition was sampled with a tuned exclusion, and Taylor's theorem with
φ‴(η/2) = 0 proves it with 99% to spare (the referee's lesson). Rerun everything a changed function feeds — the radii, not only the
branch and bound. And a certificate's cost is set by how a difference is enclosed: near a moving saddle F − F(η/2) must be one centred
form.

**Verdicts (D3cu).** Reproducibility exact; every quoted number the md's; κ′ − κ, SQ, the window masses, the gap and the null-cluster
row reproduce. No major issue. Minors: **round 97's premise was wrong, and the round-97 text inherited it (a negative result)** — the
line c = c* is invariant only for samples exactly symmetric about c*: A's six unpaired samples carry f*/A ≈ 5·10⁻⁶⁰³ at σ*/σ₀ = 0.25 (0 only
in double) and 2.3·10⁻³⁸ at 1, linspace's roundoff drifts c on the line in double, the saddle amplifies either within finite s, and the
held runs are BDF's, at the implicit step's fixed point −d/λ of the drift; the invariance and the saddle provable as a lemma; NULL_TOL not

conditions inside a comment. Cosmetic: the cap's gap incompletely justified (29 of 30 unassigned with an unused kernel; the 1.15 a shared

**Lesson.** "Invariant up to 10⁻³⁸" is not invariance when the state is a saddle: the asymmetry's logarithm over the unstable rate is a
finite time. Prove invariance for the exactly symmetric problem and state the problem as posed as its perturbation; before calling a held
state the flow, compare the held offset with the implicit step's fixed point −d/λ of the drift (here it matched to 2%) (the referee's
lesson). An assert on stored data does not kill a mutant of the code that wrote the data: test the job when it is cheap. And a referee's
proposed fix is a hypothesis to check like any other — round 97's was wrong, and the next round found it.

tabulate each term's sign across σ/h before relying on it. And in floating point "invariant on exactly symmetric samples" does not keep a
computed flow on a saddle: summation roundoff seeds both problems alike, so the exit time, not the invariance, is the observable.

| D3cy-3 | minor | Tests | `test_round104_part_v_recomputed_pinned_and_in_ball_arithmetic`: three boxes and a thin slice (317 boxes, 105839 segments) pinned in float and in ball arithmetic; \|∇C\| ≤ h′(\|σ\|) sampled, with equality where \|Re σ\| < 1 < \|σ\|; `cert_seg_ball` against the float bound and `cert_E`; the rigorous radius at the true π/2; z₀ = cert_b(R2) captured; b outside the disc rejected in ball arithmetic though the float path passes; the real path cut at 1.5ε₀ rejected; a failed rigorous bound or a short float radius planted; forced splits tiling the band exactly; CERT_BANDS contiguous with DOM_BB; a 10⁻⁶ gap and an unrigorous end piece rejected by `v_lines`; r* floored at 1.99 (W19); the exact ratio. `tools/mutants/round104_D61_own.py`: 21 mutants (the referee's unsound Y02, Y03, Y05, Y07, Y16, Y18, Y21, Y22, Y24, Y31 and W19, adapted, and 10 of the ball code); the tests kill 16 at the first run and Y18, B03, B04, B10 after planted inputs; B02 (ℓ at its lower end in the ball bound) changes it below double resolution: equivalent |
| D3cy-4 | cosmetic | The redundant term | `cert_seg_parts`: \|∇_σC\| ≤ h′(\|σ\|) (beyond \|Re σ\| = 1 \|∇C\|² = h′² − 4(\|Re σ\| − 1)(1 − \|Re σ\|/\|σ\|²)); the bands 760, 2011, 10658 boxes (160111, 946644, 9581078 segment bounds; 288 s with the recheck); D61's New: the cost near the real axis, where the domination's branch and bound does not close either |

| D3cy-6 | cosmetic | Stale text | (iv)'s proof "(by it for r < 0.9900, with V, conditionally on P beyond)", "inside \|η\| ≤ 1.995 when r < 0.9900"; HANDOFF's D‴.61 state and test count |

**Lesson.** A floating-point certificate whose terms are monotone is one step from a rigorous one: rerun the same formula in ball
arithmetic — here 77 million bounds in half an hour, the rigorous excess 3·10⁻¹⁴ — and ship the rerun, not the claim. Prove the tightest
bound you can and test each term where it binds: a redundant term multiplied the cost four- to six-fold and made unsound mutants
equivalent. When a computation shows a weaker condition than a definition states, restate the definition as the proof uses it. And a
certificate's tests must recompute it against stored values, or an unsound change that only makes it cheaper passes unseen (the
referee's lessons).

## Round 106 (adversarial review of Proposition D‴.59 as revised after round 103, 2026-11-01)

**Design.** One referee, not modifying the repository. D3da: Proposition D‴.59 as revised after round 103 — the held runs as the
computed problem's own state, the exit times, the lemma's sign scan, `mirror_asym` — at 5ee87f7 (`review/REVIEW_round106_D3da.md`). The
referee:
- regenerated the md byte for byte, ran the 52 tests, and reran 13 jobs bit-identically (A2E, four A2, H, H3, HP, HL);
- located the zero of ċ at the held states in double and in 50-digit arithmetic on the double data;
- integrated the flow from c* with DOP853, RK45, LSODA, scipy's BDF and Radau at several tolerances, and with fixed-step RK4 in double
  and long double, on A's samples and on exactly symmetric ones, from several seeds, with the Jacobian's spectrum along the route;
- recomputed the lemma's terms by finite differences against the truncated expansion, on a fine σ/h grid;
- recomputed `mirror_asym` against a bottleneck matching, all active kernels and the fitted function's odd part, with H3 unpolished and
  HL's loops in their whole state;
- ran the round's 15 mutants, 25 of its own and 3 at job level; web searches.

**Verdicts (D3da).** Reproducibility exact; every added number the md's and reproduced; the location of the held state right to the ulp
(50-digit zeros 8.12 and 9.57 ulps); the lemma's expansion right with slips, its weight right; the tests strong (every printing mutant
killed by the md-from-raw test). No major issue. Minors: **the exit's seed on A's samples is the data's, not roundoff's** — the time does
not move with precision, integrator or tolerance and every exit goes downward, while on exactly symmetric samples it moves, flips or never
comes (the principal finding); **the hold is LSODA's step sequence**, neither generic to implicit methods (scipy's BDF and Radau leave)
nor exclusive to them (a small-step RK4 in double holds by absorption); **the mirror sentence overgeneralises** and `mirror_asym` (the
nearest image) is not a distance to the fixed-point subspace ({a, a, Ra} gives 0). Cosmetic: the lemma's wording (the overshoot condition,
the remainder O((h/σ)²φ₂), the least-squares overshoot of the neighbours' order); the "9.9 ulps" the double sum's; stale text (the md's C
sentence, "a saddle in c" unconditionally, Fenichel); a hard-coded exact-start clause.

**Lesson.** A seed that survives a change of integrator and tolerance, and that the symmetric problem reproduces when started at the
posed problem's offset, belongs to the problem; one that moves or flips belongs to the computation — record the exit's direction, not
only its time (the referee's lesson, its long-double test not rerun here). A held state needs more than one solver: LSODA's hold is its
step sequence. And a fixed-point-subspace claim needs a bijective matching, all of the state, and a gauge-invariant check: here the
polished end's asymmetry sits in spikes narrower than the spacing, its function symmetric on the samples.

**Lesson.** A bracket that fails at every proved case is a symptom, not neutral evidence: on the fast branch the calibration is how the
deviation shrinks as the fit window moves out in K, and one rule's outlier is better printed as an outlier, with its ratio to the proved
maximum, than folded into a bound (the referee's lesson). Outward rounding is a property of every printed bound and range, not only of
those a referee named: sweep the bound-printing lines for `:.1e` and `:.4f` once, and give a range's two ends opposite directions.

**Lesson.** Before splitting an effect into ingredients, scan the one continuous variable they may share: "the centres at their period
means" and "the instantaneous centre" were two samples of kernel 1's centre at the restart against a per-window threshold, and fixed
offsets at a second per run show it at once (the referee's lesson). A restart's "reduced" base must be checked against the alarm it
reduces: a variant built on the fitted state instead silently answered another question. And a clause that says "implied by X" must
check X.

reversed order —, and to the arithmetic when such a change removes or reverses it; a start at a matched offset checks only the order of
magnitude on a logarithmic scale (the referee's lesson). A symmetry claim about a fit needs the function of the kernels that make it, on a
grid that resolves them: on the samples a fit's odd part is its residual's, and between them it is whatever invisible spikes the state
carries.

status line changes in the same commit.

| D3dg-5 | cosmetic | Tests | `test_round106_the_exit_s_conclusion…` extended: A's exact-sum and reversed exits upward (T03), the seeded run 1% off or reversed, the long-double exit moving with the tolerance, A's double runs 3% off, long double only 2% later, the offset start's time no condition; `test_round112_…`: the long-double exit at 3A (0.04827–0.04828 at both tolerances), the seed 2.3–2.45 times the held offset and the seeded run within 10⁻⁵, the symmetric long-double exit > 10% later, the width split (11 kernels, < 2·10⁻⁹) against the 0.95% threshold (> 10⁻³), the md's sentence. `tools/mutants/round112_D59_own.py`: 12 mutants and a control — 10 killed (V07, the flip in long double only, and V08, the long-double tolerances unchecked, after planted inputs), V09 (the width split at 2h: the gap is a factor 40, so equivalent on the data) and V12 (a one-sided difference for λ: the seed moves by O(10⁻⁹) relative) equivalent |

**Lesson.** A change of the arithmetic tests a seed only if it could have removed it: on exactly symmetric data exact sums and reversed
order are identities. The levers that separate the data's seed from the arithmetic's are precision and planting — in long double the
arithmetic's exit moved and flipped while A's did not, and the data's drift carried along the route, planted in the symmetric problem,
reproduced A's exit to 10⁻⁶ (the referee's lesson, adopted). A threshold that splits kernels needs a gap; split by width against the
samples' spacing, where the data fix the function.

proof" accurate; round 110's fixes work, their mutants killed on assertions. No major issue; no proved claim changes. Minors: **VC's
account of what remains understates it** — the remainder is not uniform in φ (relative −ε(2φ² + O(1)) near the saddle: −0.249 …
−200.26 at φ = 0 … 10), VC's floor turns positive on the true bound from θ ≈ √(ε/2) (ε = 10⁻³, φ = 25), and at θ = √εψ another limit

own — so the referee's negative finding became a sharper route: four regimes, each limit's negative path proved, the uniform certificates per regime left.

**Verdicts (D3dh).** Reproducibility exact; every new number right but one inward bound (5.85·10⁻⁹); the tier "proved by D‴.61 (iv)
for t < 0.9900, both steps rigorous in ball arithmetic" earned. No major issue. Minors: **"calibrated by the proved rule" is not a
calibration** — the threshold 3 was set with the data's 2.70 in hand; at the same τ/σ = 2 and window the proved rules' biases differ by
up to 29 times and the published calibrator is the smallest; a proved rule relabelled as unproved is rejected ("up to 29 times: NOT");
the later window's "as the proved rule's" is window geometry (a pure K⁻⁴ and K⁻³ remainder gives 2.533 and 2 for any rule); at τ/σ = ¼
no calibrator can exist —; **the outlier's four-term deviation is a transient, not a bias** — its residual falls by (h(τ²/v)/t(v))² =
0.850630 per kernel, the formula's other branch, and with it modelled the limit is within 6.5·10⁻¹⁶ —; the verdict's logic (calibrated
while its necessary condition fails, the calibrator unchecked, plants never through the 25-digit errors, "2 of the 1"). Cosmetic: tests
(12 md-only kills), V's contiguity with DB unpinned, residues.

|---|---|---|---|

**Lesson.** A calibration by a known case needs the known case to share the unknown one's error structure, and more than one known
case; the cheap test is to relabel a proved rule as unproved (the referee's lesson). When adding terms to a fit makes its limit worse,
look for a term outside the basis: here the formula's own second argument predicted the missing transient's rate to four digits, and a
float t(v) hid the six-term level — exact inputs before exact fits.

**Lesson.** A convergence test needs the check a calibration does — run it on a known case — and a criterion is better relative to the
fit's own next change than to the target (the referee's lesson, adapted). When a new basis term fixes a fit, derive its form and apply
to the enlarged model the diagnostic that exposed the gap: the transient model, too, has a next order.

|---|---|---|---|

**Lesson.** A control that starts from a state other than the run's measures that state: an earlier start must carry the run's own state,
and an effect seen only with a borrowed state is the borrowed state's (here round 114's "neither"). Merge the samples into the scan before
testing them against it — a check that looks only outside the bracket cannot see inside it (the referee's lessons, adapted).

arithmetic's only if the data are the stored ones, and every comparison beside it (the double runs, the 50-digit zero) must use the same

11 ln 2, not the percentages (the referee's lessons).

  its branch, every handoff in its connector, 5369 outer segments sampled;
- ran 37 mutants of the (patched) certificate against the certificate's own checks and its independent check, and corrected the negative
  controls' harness.

**Verdicts (D3dp).** **D3dp-1 (major, soundness): as submitted the certificate is not a proof on the whole annulus** — in the η-box [1.995,

correctness assumed: the outer piece 76 η-boxes and 5193 segments, every identity right, every rigour-relevant line right, the independent
check passing (all E < 0, the largest −6.25·10⁻⁴⁷; true − certified ≤ −3.05·10⁻¹⁶ inside; outer true − bound ≤ −2.19·10⁻⁵). Consequences:

(c_need(r)² = 4r ln(1/r)/(1 − r) < 4); D‴.58's sharp constant for every σ*/σ and t(v) for every rule with a frame. Minors: **no check
exercises the outer handoff** ("coverage complete" rested on the inner pieces); **the negative controls' harness is vacuous** (its closed
form drops −P₀₊², so it rejects the true cap too); **the self-checks under-assert** (validate's B0 never asserts; the samplers assert

**Lesson.** A NaN is not an empty interval: every float taken out of a ball that decides the certificate's shape — whether a segment
exists, an interval's ends — must be checked finite. Sample the joints, not only the pieces: coverage inside each piece cannot see a hole
between them. Run a negative control beside its positive twin, and make every self-check assert what it prints (the referee's lessons).
And the adoption was right to wait for this round: the certificate as submitted was not a proof.

(the referee's). When a check is introduced, plant the mutant it must catch itself — here the raw pin stopped every unsound joint while the
new check printed "0 outside". And a proof in balls of an inequality that is tight at a box's edge needs the edge's exact value, not the
hull's lower end: Y = arg η at the cap's corner was undecidable until θ's exact ends were used.

the spread; and name a resolution after what moves it (the referee's lessons).

draws the arithmetics' prefactors differ; the scaling is now stated as an interval with its systematic spread, and the outlier was
replicated before being named.

## D‴.40: the early-phase gap (round 147's open item, 2026-11-05)

**Design.** Round 147 left one discrepancy open: in Part E's uncorrected 'correlated E' loop the first mass at 2·10⁴ slow units sat 2.5
errors above Katzenberger's SDE ensemble on 36 new seeds (Part G), the third 2.6 below. Four explanations were tested in
`exp_gauge_noise.py` Part I (raw key I; sections A–H and keys A–H unchanged). The work was organised as follows.
- **The loop.** It is integrated in batches of 48 (`i_runs`). The drift comes from `gauge_batch`, and each seed's draws are those of
  run_dithered: Part G's and Part E's records are reproduced to 1.2·10⁻¹⁴.
- **The decomposition.** Each run's log-masses are split exactly by the gauge identity into a boundary term, the noise's martingale term
  (mean zero), the noise's drift −τ_kg′_k, the box's term, the cohesion's term and the Euler chain's bias (residual 3.4·10⁻¹⁴).
- **Runs.** 192 new seeds (500–691); the same seeds without the box; the same seeds and draws from the positions' equilibrated state.
- **Calibration.** The box's term at fixed masses against W_1 (`i_fixed`).
- **Katzenberger's SDE variants.** Steps 50, 10 and 2; without walls (`i_field` on an extended grid); with the measured box term through
  Katzenberger's projection at γ (`i_field_row`'s Π, `i_sde`).
- **Statistics.** Holm's adjustment over the recorded times, and the martingale term regressed out.

CPU: about 48 min in all, of which 24 min for Part I.

**Findings.** The gap is a fluctuation of those seeds' noise, not a departure from the limit.
- **Statistics.** The 192 new seeds give z = +1.42, +1.80, +0.68 at 5·10³, 10⁴ and 2·10⁴. The smallest Holm-adjusted p is 0.2151, against
  0.0363 for the 36 seeds. The 36 seeds lie 0.0085 ± 0.0041 above the 192.
- **The martingale term.** Its expectation is exactly zero. It adds +0.0176 ± 0.0067 to the 36 seeds' first mass, +0.0327 ± 0.0115 to
  Part E's 12 and +0.0050 ± 0.0034 to the 192.
- **With that term regressed out** (correlation 0.700–0.987), the 192 seeds' first mass is known to ±0.0002–0.0009. Its displacement is
  0.90 ± 0.06, 0.84 ± 0.08 and 1.06 ± 0.14 times Katzenberger's.

The four hypotheses, with their power:
- **(1) Beyond Katzenberger's limit.** The field is taken at γ = 10⁻² itself, so the finite-γ terms are already in it. Without the box,
  the loop's displacement is 0.97 ± 0.05, 0.94 ± 0.05 and 0.86 ± 0.10 times that of the wall-free SDE. Runs at γ = 3·10⁻³ and 10⁻³ were
  therefore not needed and not made.
- **(2) The start.** An equilibrated start with the same draws moves the first mass by +0.0001 ± 0.0001; the spreading estimate is
  2.1·10⁻⁴.
- **(3) The SDE.** Its means at steps 50, 10 and 2 differ by at most 0.0006. The box is a soft wall: its term equals the
  noise's drive at W_1 = 0.3050. The loop therefore rarely falls below 0.30 (0.0677 of seeds at 2·10⁴, against the SDE's 0.1003). But
  its paired effect on the mean, +0.0003 ± 0.0001, +0.0019 ± 0.0004 and +0.0060 ± 0.0008, is the reflection's (+0.0001, +0.0019,
  +0.0074). The SDE with the measured box term has the same means.
- **(4) Multiple times.** As above.

**Changes.** The changes are:
- PARADIGM D‴.40: Numerics (E), row 152, the numerics row and the roadmap's open item, which is closed.
- `exp_gauge_noise.py` Part I, with the md section appended.
- 6 tests in `tests/test_gauge_noise.py`. The existing md-from-raw test now passes Part I.
- `tools/mutants/gap40_gauge_noise_own.py`.

**Verification.**
- **Reproduction.** gauge_noise.md regenerates byte-identically from its raw (`--from-raw` on a copy, cmp). Old sections and raw keys
  A–H are unchanged; the pickles are identical.
- **Tests.** 26 pass (tests/test_gauge_noise.py, tests/test_runcache.py).
- **Mutants.** 16 mutants and a control, all killed. Q14 (the no-box runs given the box) survived the first pass and was killed by a test
  on seed 507, which leaves the box by 5·10³.
- **Number check.** Every decimal in the new D‴.40 text is printed in the md.

**Lesson.** A 2.5σ gap found in the sample that prompted the question must be retested on fresh seeds before it is explained. Where an
exact identity supplies a zero-mean term, as the gauge identity supplies the noise's martingale, regressing it out shows how much of a
sample's deviation is its noise realisation. Here it also shrank the error up to fivefold, at 5·10³. A box-free Gaussian estimate of the
box's term was off by orders of magnitude: the stiff box reshapes the tail it acts on. That term had to be measured in the boxed law.

leaves a residual, rerun at a smaller step on the same Brownian path: the chain's own term misses the step's effect on the other terms,
and a restoring drift evaluated at the measured state can cancel an offset that a neutral direction accumulates.

## D‴.40: the missing O(γ²τ) drift (after round 153, 2026-11-05)

**Design.** Part K (round 153) left one item open. In 'nonlinear only' (the centres and widths dithered, the amplitudes noise-free,
γ = 0.01, τ = 0.0001) the loop's secular displacement was far below Katzenberger's O(γ²τ) drift path. Four explanations were tested in
`exp_gauge_noise.py` Part M (raw key M; sections A–L and keys A–L unchanged; `review/RESEARCH_note_gamma2_drift.md`).
- **(a) The prediction.** It is computed three ways at 1/3: the linearised positions' antisymmetric correlation in closed form (`m_ou`);
  `limit_drift`; and the second differences of the limit map Φ (`m_limit`: the noise-free loop by RK4; `m_fd`).
- **(b) Part K's records with the exact limit map.** Y = Φ(state) at every 5th record of the second half (`m_lim_K`), in place of Part K's
  first-order offset (1). The offset with the fit's motion with the masses is (I − M)⁻¹(1) (`m_offset_lin`).
- **(c) The loop's own rate.** 48 new seeds (800–847), 200000 slow units from the exact fit, at γ = 0.01 and 0.003. Each run is two Euler
  chains at Δt and Δt/2 on one Brownian path (`m_loop`), and the rate is Richardson's 2r(Δt/2) − r(Δt) of Y between 20000 and 200000.
- **(d) The antisymmetric correlation at fixed masses.** At τ = 3e-05, 0.0001 and 0.0003, with the same coupling (`m_fixed`, `m_anti`).
- **(e) Part K's shortfall term by term.** The four terms are Part K's residual, the offset's error, the step correction's excess over
  (c)'s step effect, and the rest.

CPU: about 95 min for Part M, in one process.

**Findings.** The loop carries the drift. Part K missed it mainly through its estimator.
- **(a)** The prediction stands. Φ's second differences agree with `limit_drift` to 0.0016 at γ = 0.01 (0.0242 at 0.001, in the small third
  class). The closed form is −0.01368, +0.01237, +0.00131 per γ²τ, against `limit_drift`'s −0.01387, +0.01263, +0.00125 at γ = 1e-05.
- **(b)** The first-order offset ignores the fit's motion with the masses: −diag M = 0.3135, 0.0560, 0.0938 at 1/3. Per record,
  |W − Y − (1)| reaches 8.6e-04, while |W − Y − (I − M)⁻¹(1)| is at most 1.4e-05. With Y, the displacement less (2) is 0.70, 0.63, 1.07 of
  the path.
- **(c)** The Richardson rate is 0.79 ± 0.08, 0.81 ± 0.09 of Katzenberger's at γ = 0.01 (z = +2.6, −2.1) and 0.79 ± 0.09, 0.86 ± 0.08 at
  0.003, on the same draws. From γ = 0.01 to 0.003 it grows 1.44 ± 0.02, 1.61 ± 0.04, against Katzenberger's 1.43, 1.52. The step's own
  effect on the rate, −0.00730 ± 0.00009, +0.01071 ± 0.00010, is as large as the drift.
- **(d)** At fixed masses the correlation is 1.08 ± 0.20, 1.07 ± 0.13 of the closed form at τ = 3e-05 and 0.86 ± 0.08, 0.93 ± 0.10 at
  0.0001; at 0.0003 it is undetermined. The antisymmetric share is at most 0.0341.
- **(e)** As shares of the path, Part K's residual is 0.15 ± 0.19, 0.15 ± 0.07 and the offset's error 0.55 ± 0.14, 0.48 ± 0.07. The step
  correction's excess is 0.09 ± 0.02, 0.08 ± 0.03, and the rest 0.20 ± 0.09, 0.29 ± 0.06. The rest is the loop's own shortfall, not a
  fluctuation of Part K's 12 seeds (z = +0.1, −0.9 against (c)). It matches (d)'s at τ = 0.0001 (z = −0.6, −0.8).
- **Open.** Whether that shortfall is a finite-τ correction of the positions' law is not settled: (d) at 0.0003 is too noisy.

**Changes.** The changes are:
- `exp_gauge_noise.py` Part M, with the md section appended. Report-only fixes were made before the md was installed: the first transient
  Y(20000) − 1/3 had omitted the − 1/3, and the lines after (d) and part (e) were added.
- `results/chaos/gauge_noise.md` and `gauge_noise_raw.npz` (new key M).
- 8 tests in `tests/test_gauge_noise.py`; the md-from-raw tests now pass M. One threshold was corrected to the data: Φ's second differences
  against `limit_drift`, 0.002 at γ = 0.01 and 0.03 at 0.001.
- `tools/mutants/drift40_gauge_noise_own.py`.
- PARADIGM D‴.40: the Part K passage, row 152 and the numerics row, with dated markers.

**Verification.**
- **Reproduction.** gauge_noise.md regenerates byte-identically from its raw (`--from-raw` twice on a copy, cmp). Sections A–L are
  identical to the committed md, and raw keys A–L are pickle-identical.
- **Tests.** 42 pass (tests/test_gauge_noise.py, tests/test_runcache.py).
- **Mutants.** 22 mutants and a control (`tools/mutants/drift40_gauge_noise_own.py`), all killed. N14 (m_fd's Richardson weights)
  survived the first pass, since the raw stores m_fd's result. It was killed by a test that replaces the limit map with a known quartic.
- **Number check.** Every decimal in the note and in the new D‴.40 text is printed in the md.

**Lesson.** A first-order offset about a reference that itself moves with the measured quantity misses the reference's response. Where the
coupling is not small (here 0.3135, an amplitude near its saturation), use the exact map or the resolvent (I − M)⁻¹. A drift of order γ²τ
can be as small as the Euler chain's O(Δt) effect at the production step; measure it by Richardson's extrapolation on coupled chains. A
residual taken for a fluctuation must be retested on the new runs: here it was the loop's own shortfall.

round 154"); `review/RESEARCH_note_c2.md` (a dated note after Proposition A (iii), a Review-history line); `review/drafts/D61.md` (a
dated note after the round-148 upgrade). No experiment, md, raw, test or tool changed.

**Verification.** §S1's algebra re-checked independently in floating point with truncated power series at random complex points (b₁, the
γ₁ table and its sum u + u², G₁ = F₁, the ridge's Hessian and third and fourth derivatives, T_I, T_II, T_III against Wick's rule, ς₁ on
both axes, Corollary S1.4's expansion; worst deviation 1·10⁻¹⁰, rounding) and in exact rationals at the six values of Table 3 and §S1.
Builds in a scratch copy (three passes each), PDFs copied back: paper 28 pp., supplement 16 pp. (12 before); 0 errors, 0 undefined
references, 0 overfull boxes, no "??"; every existing label keeps its number in both documents. Decimal tokens (comments stripped, before
and after): the paper 76 → 76, none added or removed; the supplement 114 → 118, the new ones cross-references to the paper (4.1, 4.2,
4.9, 4.10). No model identifier added.

**Lesson.** After a hard region of a proof is replaced, re-read the statement's whole range, its trivial points included: a scaling
argument that divides by the base point fails exactly where nothing seemed to need proof. And a manuscript should carry its own proofs and
no revision history: move a companion note's proofs into the supplement, and describe superseded certificates by what they check, not by
when they were used (the referee's lessons).

## D‴.40: the finite-τ question (Part N, 2026-11-05)

**Design.** Part M left one item open: the loop carries Katzenberger's O(γ²τ) drift at only 0.79 ± 0.08, 0.81 ± 0.09 of it, and the
fixed-mass correlation fell short too at τ = 0.0001. Was that a finite-τ correction of the positions' law, or noise? `exp_gauge_noise.py`
Part N (raw key N; keys A–M and md sections A–M unchanged) calls Part M's `m_fixed` unchanged at new seeds: 32 at τ = 0.0001 (1100–1131)
and 144 at 0.0003 (1400–1543), with Part M(d)'s run lengths so that the seeds pool, and 16 at 0.001 (1300–1315). It reports the pooled
ratio (Richardson over the closed form) per τ, the new seeds against Part M(d)'s, and the weighted line through τ = 3·10⁻⁵, 10⁻⁴, 3·10⁻⁴.
CPU: about 60 min in one process (two background runs, the second resumed from the raw), plus a 3-minute pilot that was not kept.

**Findings** (first two classes).
- **Not noise.** At τ = 0.0001 the new seeds alone give 0.79 ± 0.09, 0.79 ± 0.07. Pooled, the ratio is 0.82 ± 0.06, 0.86 ± 0.06
  (z = −3.0, −2.3 against 1).
- **τ = 0.0003.** The pooled ratio is 0.19 ± 0.32, 0.49 ± 0.31. The seeds' spread there is 4.06, 3.96.
- **The line.** The slope is −0.33 ± 0.14, −0.23 ± 0.12 per 10⁻⁴ of τ (z = −2.3, −1.9). The limit τ → 0 is 1.15 ± 0.15, 1.10 ± 0.12,
  consistent with 1. A constant ratio, 0.82 ± 0.06, 0.88 ± 0.05, lies 3.2 and 2.1 errors below 1, but its χ² does not reject it
  (p = 0.07, 0.14).
- **τ = 0.001** (16 seeds) is not informative.
- **Reading.** A finite-τ correction is favoured but not established.

**Changes.**
- `exp_gauge_noise.py`: `part_N`, `n_pool`, `n_fit`, `n_ratios`, `report_N`, and `main`'s N. Part M's functions are unchanged.
- `results/chaos/gauge_noise.md` (section N appended) and `gauge_noise_raw.npz` (key N).
- `tests/test_gauge_noise.py`: 5 tests. They cover the design and the seeds' freshness, part_N's resumption, n_fit against numpy, Part
  N's numbers from the raw, and the md from the raw with A–M unchanged. The three md-from-raw tests now pass N.
- `tools/mutants/finite_tau_gauge_noise_own.py`.
- `review/RESEARCH_note_gamma2_drift.md` §3–5.
- PARADIGM D‴.40: the open-item sentence and the numerics row, with dated markers.

**Verification.**
- **Reproduction.** `--from-raw`, run twice on copies, gives byte-identical output, which matches the run's own md. Sections A–M are
  identical to the committed md, and raw keys A–M are pickle-identical.
- **Tests.** 47 pass (tests/test_gauge_noise.py, tests/test_runcache.py).
- **Mutants.** 10 mutants and a control, all killed.
- **Number check.** `tools/numcheck.py` finds only the date and 3·10⁻⁴ (printed in the md as 0.0003).

**Lesson.** Re-running the same estimator on new seeds settled whether the 10⁻⁴ shortfall was real. It did not settle the slope. The
per-seed spread grows steeply with τ, so the large-τ point that has the most leverage on the slope is also the most expensive.

## Round 156 (adversarial review of the WP1 generality study, `experiments/exp_parametrization.py` at 5083a49, 2026-11-07)

**Design.** One referee (PZ1), not modifying the repository (`review/REVIEW_round156_PZ1.md`). F1 derived independently and checked by finite
differences at three constant sets with G ≠ 1, a_max ≠ 1 and wrong-rate controls; an independent engine (LSODA, Radau, DOP853, the reduced mirror
coordinates) recomputed cells; attempts to make depth 2 pass (centre and learning rates, horizon, asymmetric starts, dictionary spacing, thresholds) and
depth 3 fail (D4, D5, K = 2, near ties); the margin analysis of the 200 targets; bit-for-bit recomputation of 96 + 84 cells of part C and 42 of the
other parts; 77 single-point mutants of `factorized_rbf.py`; the literature (Woodworth et al., Gissin et al., Pesme–Flammarion).

**Verdicts (PZ1).** F1 (the law is the Euclidean gradient flow in (α, √β, c)) confirmed. F2 (depth-3 readouts reproduce the path) partly confirmed,
overstated as worded: it is a statement against the runner-up margin — no mismatch on the 98 of 200 targets with margin ≥ 0.02. F3 (depth 2 does not
select at a practical ε) confirmed for generic off-grid targets, with its conditions: the margin inequality μ > ln(1/θ)/ln(1/ε), and 4.74 = ln(1/θ), not
a law. F4 (depth 1, fixed-step descent, Adam) confirmed. One major, nine minor, one cosmetic finding; no conclusion moved.

| id | sev. | issue | fix (where) |
|---|---|---|---|
| PZ1-1 | major | F2's set identity, order and static dormant units hold only where the runner-up margin is large (98/98 above 0.02; every mismatch below) | `margins`, `reference` store μ; part C's margin-stratified table and per-target failures; pins (`tests/test_parametrization.py`); CLAIMS §5 reworded |
| PZ1-2 | minor | 4.74 is ln(1/θ); "no practical ε" is the inequality μ > ln(1/θ)/ln(1/ε) | part D's text and rule table (agrees on 21, 21, 20, 19, 20, 21 of 21); `gap_k`, `exact_topk` in `analyse` (the referee's top-K counts 0, 1, 10, 13, 20, 21 reproduced); the dictionary-spacing sweep is the referee's, not committed |
| PZ1-3 | minor | "A–H, J cannot trigger the Radau fallback" (message of 5083a49) is false: E[3] (4.3·10⁶ evaluations) and J[8] did; the raw held two versions of one computation; usage unrecorded | `radau_pieces`, `aborted_nfev` per cell; B, C, D, E, J rerun with the final engine (single version; 104 of C's 1200 cells used the fallback); STIFF_BUDGET, MAX_SECS in the md header |
| PZ1-4 | minor | the wall-clock limit was lowered (400 → 120 s) after the runs; status depended on machine speed | MAX_SECS = 900 as a safety net above every cell (the slowest J cell 149 s median); E, J rerun |
| PZ1-5 | minor | non-ok cells drop out of denominators silently; no report test with a non-ok cell | the md header prints, per part, cells run and cells not ok (B: 1 — D5 at 10⁻¹⁰, a recorded solver failure); `test_the_report_states_the_status_of_every_cell` |
| PZ1-6 | minor | truncated failing-cell list; "max τ err." is a record-grid artefact; reference flags discarded; P0u/P4/D1 not in C | failures grouped per target (34 of 200); 95th percentile and a note on the grid; flags stored and printed; P0u/P4 wording in CLAIMS |
| PZ1-7 | minor | 23 of 77 mutants survive; G and a_max never varied; semantics unpinned | 14 new tests: the identity at three constant sets with wrong-rate controls; `tau_rel` (max), `order_equal` (spurious units), `dormant_wmax` (peak), `gap_k`, `exact_topk`; Adam on P0 with the default ε_adam; an empty solver result — **which found a second crash** (`Z[a+1:a+1] = Y.T[:0]`, shape (0,) into (0, 63)), fixed; the budget; the mutation run was not repeated |
| PZ1-8 | minor | "depth ≥ 3" tested at depth 3 only | `PowerN` (D4, D5) in part B: clean (D4 to 10⁻¹⁰, D5 to 10⁻⁸) |
| PZ1-9 | minor | part G's random α(0) rows are not the logarithmic regime | **not done** (the referee's ±a₀ pairs: P0 depth-2-like at a₀ = 0.3, ε = 10⁻⁶); wording fixed in CLAIMS |
| PZ1-10 | cosmetic | header "10³" (it binds from a ratio of 10); "later or earlier"; Adam at 10⁻⁶; test count | `report()` header; CLAIMS |
| PZ1-11 | minor (Paper 17) | l.127 "not a Euclidean one": in (α, √β, c) the metric is Euclidean | recorded (CLAIMS §0 D8); **Paper 17 not yet corrected** |

**Lesson.** A limit statement checked on a random sample must be reported against the parameter that measures the distance from the limit: the
runner-up margin against ε^½ for depth ≥ 3 and against ln(1/θ)/ln(1/ε) for depth 2 — a bare fraction (166 of 200) hid a clean 98 of 98. Every
budget that can change a cell's status (wall-clock, evaluations, a solver switch) must be fixed before the runs and recorded in each cell. And the
test a referee asks for is worth writing even when the code "obviously works": the empty-result test found a second crash one line after the first fix.

## Round IS2 (2026-11-07): the separated-regime theorem and its proof outline (coordinator's reading of the verbatim report `REVIEW_roundIS2.md`)

Scope: `supp_sep.tex` (private paper workspace) and `experiments/exp_separated_regime.py`. The referee found no counterexample to the structure of the argument in about 1100 runs
(1-D and 2-D, amplitude ratios up to 10, lattice spacings 0.83 and 2.5 sigma) and found the time-accuracy clause false as worded and the proven regime above every tested separation.

| # | severity | finding | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| IS2-1 | blocker as worded | the entry-time error is O(Gamma(Delta - h sqrt(n)/2)), not O(Gamma(Delta)): the best kernel can be up to h/2 closer to the neighbour | statement now O(delta_Delta); the experiment reports the error against Gamma(Delta - h/2) (largest ratio 0.99 at 5-8 sigma, slope 1.01); `terr` only where the entries are the prediction's |
| IS2-2 | major | the proof's own constants put Delta_0 at 8 sigma or more (12-14 sigma with delta_Delta), above every tested separation; the 5 Gamma gate is lattice-specific | text and abstract say so; the gate is replaced by min(mu0, gap) > Gamma(Delta - h/2) (379 of 379), labelled an empirical law; the experiment is described as a test of the structure |
| IS2-3 | major | Lemma (iii) (coupled entry) is a sketch and its hypothesis ("nondegenerate minimum of its own fit") is not what step 4 supplies; the cross term of the splitting was incomplete | Lemma restated (critical point of the fit to the whole target; delta_0 not computed; corrected splitting) in `supp_theory.tex` and `supp_sep.tex`; (H3) is "for delta <= delta_0" |
| IS2-4 | major | (H4) for every level is not what the monotonicity lemma gives | (H4) at each fixed level with a threshold depending on the level; Thm 1(c) needs fixed levels only |
| IS2-5 | major | (H2) is the mobility-weighted Hessian; lambda_0 mixed units | lambda_0 = Z min{m_w, Lambda_0 G m A_min^2/(2 sigma^2)}, the model constants listed among the dependencies |
| IS2-6 | minor | uniqueness in a ball of radius sigma is false (the Hessian bound holds to about half a width) | Newton-Kantorovich radius r_NK ~ (sigma, A_min)/2 in the scaled norm |
| IS2-7 | major | quantifiers: fixed local data and random positions; h/sigma enters as exp(h^2 n/16 sigma^2); equal walls are not only notation; finite dictionary, fixed target; scale non-invariance | all stated in the theorem and Remark (b), (c) |
| IS2-8 | major as wording | "(H1-H4) hold" and "proved" over-claim | replacement wording applied to the abstract, introduction (contribution 2 and scope), conclusion, theorem; Thm 1's proof is called an outline |
| IS2-9 | minor | step 2/3 details: far-class bound and induction hypothesis, dimension of the error expression, mu_0/2 for the far class, 2^n ties at a cell corner | corrected in the proof |
| IS2-10 | minor | notation clashes (g gap vs drive, sigma_k vs sigma, A_min) | gap renamed varpi (code: `gap`), drive q in the lemma |
| IS2-11 | minor | experiment presentation: terr mixed events at <= 4 sigma | terr defined only where the entry sequence is the decoupled prediction's |

**Lesson.** A perturbative statement has to be checked against the size of the perturbation parameter it is *actually* small in: delta_Delta carries the offset of the best kernel and a polynomial factor, and with the proof's own constants it is not small until 12 sigma.
The experiment that supports the structure (the decoupled prediction, the first-order error) is not a test of the regime where the theorem applies, and must say so.

**Lesson.** A diagnosis that rests on label-free evidence (a residual scale, a stamp misfit) must be tested against a world in which the cause is removed by construction (an exact-stamp synthetic frame): the referee's control found that the
kernel misfit explains the residual excess but not the whole loss.

Three major findings concern what the result may be called, and a defect of the path. Dispositions as of this commit (open items marked):

| # | severity | finding | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| REP-1 | major | P1 "confirmed on held-out frames" is one frame and two patches; its sign depends on the uncorrected 0.25 px truth offset of that frame (aligned: -0.015 [-0.043, 0.012]); the a priori default secondary is a Monte Carlo accident (lower end +1e-5, positive for 7 % of other seeds); the all-six row is diluted by four zeros | the paper states P1 as "positive under the declared scoring on one frame (one patch ties), not robust to the truth offset" and no longer "confirmed"; `repeat.md` and the plan are frozen and unchanged; the referee's controls are being ported into a tested experiment (`exp_astro_repeat_sens.py`): OPEN until it reports |
| REP-2 | major | the "entry cap" runs are an enter/exit limit cycle of one lattice point in `imaging.sliding_path` (a defect, not a censoring): 3 repeat default runs, both M92 default runs, 6 of the 12 development-grid paths that `choose` ranked as valid rows | verified by the coordinator (m2r3 (110, 501), a priori default: lattice point (110, 54) enters and exits 2345 times at tau 2.18969 after 155 distinct entries; reproduced in 12 s with `max_entries` 200; the instrumented block fit shows the mechanism: the entrant's coefficient is 0 although the correlation at its lattice start is positive). A guarded copy `src/core/imaging_guard.py` (a lattice point that has exited twice at one entry time is barred; `imaging.py` stays hash-frozen) is used for 11 labelled re-runs, a check of every other published astronomy path (identical or not), the corrected development table (is the frozen configuration still the argmax?) and the corrected rows (M92 and repeat defaults, P1 secondaries): DONE (`results/astro/cyclefix.md`): the development argmax is unchanged (sigma_b 3, r_ex 1.2, kappa 2, pooled F 0.5615; Outcome A); the M2 tuned frozen-configuration rows on three of four test patches are identical with the guard, so the headline M2 numbers stand; 27 of the 65 other published paths are identical, 38 differ (usually by F < 0.005, at most about 0.025); two development paths (hp 8, r_ex 0.8) still reach the cap and some paths show residual multi-entry behaviour (up to 23 entries of one point); corrected rows: M92 default pooled F 0.147 (kappa 5) and 0.137 (BIC) against 0.150 as run, still a loss against crowdsource default; repeat default pooled 0.305 (BIC 0.320) against 0.289 (0.306); P1 default and BIC secondaries become not confirmed (0.006 [-0.019, 0.030], 0.019 [-0.004, 0.042]), the tuned P1 line is unchanged; SMLM spot check: one activation in 640 frame-fits, one frame changed. The corrected rows are post hoc and are labelled so in the paper |

| REP-4 | minor | P2's scope: crowdsource ahead of the ISS at m < 20 on one patch; the ISS is less pure than photutils at m < 22 and has 3923 unmatched detections; "tuned" baselines are post-filters without a high-pass front end; six patches are four sky windows; no photutils-default pairs | sensitivity experiment (depth cuts, tolerances, pairs); the baselines-with-the-ISS-front-end experiment (F7, running) answers the front-end point; scope sentence in the supplement; purity already in Table 2 |
| REP-5 | minor | P3 has no verdict and is mixed (the scale improves most where F does not) | printed per readout by the sensitivity experiment; stated in the supplement |
| REP-6 | minor | "scaling the lengths by the seeing does not help" holds for the tuned configuration only (at the default the scaled run removes the three capped runs) | restricted to the tuned configuration in the paper; frame-level rows from the sensitivity experiment; the default's gain is tied to REP-2 |
| REP-7 | minor | the freeze hashes named functions only, not the decision code; some frozen modules were edited (docstrings, `report()`) during the run | stated; no harm found by the referee; cannot be redone for this run |

**Lesson.** A flag that a run was stopped by a cap is a symptom to be explained before it is called censoring: the cap of 2500 entries was reported in three tables as "censored" for two rounds while it hid a limit cycle that the stopping time could not end. And a
held-out label does not make a small effect robust: the sign of the one confirmed gain depended on a 0.25 px mapping offset that the plan had declared and left uncorrected.
